To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Cowpea is an excellent model species for drought stress studies, as it is highly tolerant to water deficit, 2) Cowpea plants acclimate to drought stress through a progressive adjustment in metabolism and physiology, 3) Osmoproteantion is more important than osmotic adjustment for drought resistance in cowpea, and 4) Cowpea cultivars differ in the extent to which they adjust metabolically, which may account for their differential drought tolerance.
the cowpea plants were able to acclimate to drought by accumulating proline, galacinol and a quercitin derivative.

drought stress tolerance in cowpea plants is associated with the accumulation of proline, galacitinol and quercetin derivative in the leaves and roots, and that the accumulation of these metabolites is positively correlated to yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the metabolic and physiological responses that allow plants to cope with drought, and how they can be used to improve crop performance.
the role of metabolites as a strategy to cope with water stress in plants, and the importance of metabolomics as a tool to identify key metabolites for improving drought stress resistance in crops.
the physiological mechanisms underlying the osmotic adjustments of cowpea plants, and how they contribute to drought resistance and yield improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drought tolerance in cowpea is a result of a combination of physiological, biochemical, and metabolic changes.
drought tolerance in cowpea plants was achieved via a combination of osmotic and osmoprotective mechanisms.
the cowpea metabolome is highly plastic, but also highly specific in its response to drought, which may be a key feature for the species’ survival and adaptation to drought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the osmoprotectant strategy is the main strategy for drought tolerance in cowpea, with the osmolyte strategy as a secondary one.

the cowpea cultivars studied were able to cope with drought stress through the accumulation of compatible solutes, which were mainly organic compounds, and that these compounds were more likely to be used as osmoprotectants in the aerial parts, rather than osmoprotecting solutes.
osmoprotection and osmoadaptation are not mutually exclusive and the ability of plants for osmotic adjustment is not necessarily related to osmoprotection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metabolites can have different roles during the progression of stress.
metabolomics can be used as a powerful tool in the search of osmoprotectants for improving drought resistance and yield in cowpea.
the metabolic responses to drought in cowpea are complex and that a multifactorial approach is necessary to understand their physiological significance.
